payout_quote: Official Redbubble Help: 'Let's say you are in the Standard tier, and you earn $40 from orders shipped between the first day and the last day of the month. A platform fee of 50% will be deducted, and you will be paid the remaining balance of $20.' And: 'Now let's say you are in the Premium tier, and you earn $25 from orders shipped between the first day and the last day of the month. A platform fee of 20% will be deducted, and you will be paid the remaining balance of $20.' And: 'You are paid for every shipped sale you make after your earnings reach the payment threshold of $10, £10, or €10.' 'The payout process begins at the beginning of the month, and the payment should land in your account by the 15th.'
steps: Create a free Redbubble artist account and open your shop.
Upload your designs to products; set your product markup (artist margin).
Customers purchase; Redbubble prints, ships, and handles service.
Earn your margin minus the platform fee (50% Standard, 20% Premium); paid monthly by the 15th after reaching the $10 threshold.
catches: Redbubble takes a 50% platform fee on the Standard tier (20% on Premium) — you keep only half your margin unless you qualify for Premium.
An excess markup fee applies to product markup above 20% at point of sale.
$10 minimum payment threshold; paid monthly by the 15th.
Highly variable: most artists earn little; income depends on designs, traffic, and sales volume.
biggest_catch: Redbubble takes 50% of your earnings on the Standard tier — you keep only half your artist margin — and with a $10 monthly threshold plus monthly payouts, most casual uploaders earn little or nothing.
eligibility: 18+; original artwork you have rights to.
timing: Monthly payouts by the 15th after reaching $10 threshold.
